decisions: A1: EDGAR index pages link inline-XBRL primary documents as /ix?doc=...; the first fetch saved the viewer stub (6 KB) instead of the filing. Fixed by stripping the /ix?doc= prefix and re-fetching all documents before any A2 output existed.
A1: all documents fetched fresh from EDGAR (no copying from the project corpus). 10-Q/10-K: primary document only. 8-K: main document plus every EX-99.x exhibit.

A2: defined terms were taken in a single pass from sentences hit by the listed anchors. A first run iterated to a fixed point (defined terms defining further terms); it was replaced before A4/A5 because 'an anchored sentence' most literally means one hit by the listed anchors. Flagged for review.

A2: the cleaner's block unit is a line of the cleaned text (tone.sentences splits per line); para_id is the line index. A heading is a non-empty line of 12 or fewer whitespace tokens whose last character is not . ! or ?; its passage is the next non-empty line. A passage merging windows from several anchors joins its anchor types with '|'.
A2: table membership = the anchor line's normalized text equals a line of extract_text() applied to an HTML <table> in the same document.
A2: the cleaner's MIN_CHARS skip (an indexing rule in clean_doc) was not applied; no exit document was short.
A5: the subagent noted the instruction conflict ('Do not use any tools' vs 'Read only that one file') and used Read/Grep on the blind file only.
A5: one passage exceeds 1,900 characters; the subagent's Read tool may truncate very long lines. The subagent reported reading every row.

A6: F1 runs before case-insensitive dedup; duplicates keep the first spelling and accumulate subagent exit_ids/quotes. F2 sentence-initial = first token of a tone.sentences sentence within a normalized passage; tokens split on hyphens as in term_regex. per_exit_counts = number of exit passages matched.
A6 was run three times on identical locked inputs (code-only re-runs after aligning the F2 tokenizer); results identical. A5 ran once.
